title: What Is Taken to Have Already Been Taken Off a Healthy Options Card
content:
Where a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card programme is closed, what has already been taken off the card is read from the card's own entries taking money back.

**When the figure is fixed.** The balance given up on the closing day is worked out only after the allowance of the benefit period whose life has ended stands taken back on the card.

What has already been taken off the card is the total of the allowances taken back for want of spending, where the card carries such an allowance taken back and no balance given up at a closure; it is those allowances together with any balance already given up at a closure, where the card carries a balance given up at a closure; and it is nothing in every other case.

**The two kinds of entry.** An allowance taken back for want of spending is an entry ending a benefit period's allowance that was not used. A balance given up at a closure is an entry giving up what was left on the card when a programme was closed. Both are entries taking money off the card, and both are read from the card's own record.

- The card carries an allowance taken back for want of spending, and no balance given up at a closure: the total of those allowances taken back.
- The card carries a balance given up at a closure: those allowances together with that balance given up, whether or not any allowance was taken back for want of spending.
- The card carries neither: nothing.

**Worked through on hypothetical entries.** A card carrying allowances taken back of 46.80 USD and 30.00 USD and no balance given up at a closure: what has already been taken off is 76.80 USD. The same card also carrying a balance given up at a closure of 12.00 USD: what has already been taken off is 88.80 USD. A card carrying neither kind of entry: nothing.
